newsitem.title: FRANCE: French leaders' image a bit better in latest poll.
newsitem.headline: French leaders' image a bit better in latest poll.

text.p: The public image of French President Jacques Chirac and Prime Minister Alain Juppe has improved a little after a public relations blitz, according to a public opinion poll released on Tuesday.
The CSA poll for the weekly La Vie found that the proportion of French voters lacking confidence in Chirac fell to 52 percent in January from 55 percent a month earlier.
Similarly, the percentage of those lacking confidence in Juppe fell to 59 percent from 63 percent in December, the pollsters found.
The poll, which surveyed 1,004 individuals aged 18 or older on January 20-21, found that 38 percent retained confidence in Chirac and 31 percent in Juppe, both unchanged from last month.

The poll followed a series of Chirac television appearances, Juppe's publication of a first-person book aimed at humanising his image, and the unveiling of a presidential initiative to reform the justice system.

The leaders' popularity has been battered by record 12.7 percent unemployment, an austerity programme aimed at helping France qualify for European monetary union and criticisms that Chirac has failed to keep promises made ahead of his election as president in May 1995.
